notes: Medium. The shipped paygate repository is green and its CLI works, so there is no crash to chase: the whole difficulty is reasoning. The spec (README) contains two unconditional requirements, R4 (group totals are raw gross figures, no netting regardless of refunds or chargebacks) and R7 (any group containing a refund/chargeback must display the settled amount), which cannot both hold for an adjusted group; the shipped code 'resolves' the conflict ad hoc by netting only the groups whose names mention refunds/chargebacks, which is neither requirement and is pinned by shipped tests. The agent must read the spec and fixtures carefully, surface the contradiction, choose one coherent resolution (all-gross or all-net), implement it uniformly, update the tests that pinned the mixed behaviour, and document the decision in /app/decisions.md quoting both conflicting requirements verbatim. The verifier accepts either coherent resolution but rejects third behaviour (per-group values outside {gross, net}, a mixed rule, or an inconsistent choice across the visible and three hidden ledgers), rejects a missing/incomplete decision record, and requires the repo's own test suite to stay green. Hidden ledgers generalize over group names (including neutral names that defeat the shipped name heuristic), group counts, zero-net groups, an empty group and a large group. Reasoning depth from requirement-conflict discovery and the documented choice; debugging ambiguity from tests that pin the wrong behaviour; hidden_case_generalization from three fresh ledgers; tool breadth from git, pytest, JSON fixtures and a small Python package. No resource pressure, no safety dimension, no statefulness.
